participants: Ayla Lerner (Senior BDR, Tabs — external, not a Primal Instinct employee)
summary: Not a sales call and not a Primal Instinct team call. This is the second personal career-networking conversation in this batch by the rep labelled 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)', recorded on the same Fathom note-taker used for prospect calls and filed in the same sales folder, one day after the first. He is in Brooklyn; the counterparty is Ayla Lerner, a senior BDR at the fintech company Tabs, introduced by a mutual contact named Sean. He gives his background — 2020 economics and finance degree, Morgan Stanley wealth management, SVB tech banking — and states he wants to move into B2B enterprise tech sales, ideally at an AI company. Ayla covers her own path from investment banking and PE business development into a BDR role at Tabs, the onboarding and enablement system, call recording and CRM visibility, promotion mechanics from BDR to senior BDR to AE, quota attainment expectations, and what she considers the defining quality of top performers (urgency). She tells him Tabs does not hire senior BDRs externally, that hiring is backlogged until at least August, and offers a referral link once she checks with Sean. He confirms he intends to apply.
notable: Second external job-search call recorded on company tooling in two days, both filed in the 'Andrew Musial' sales-call folder under generic 'Impromptu Google Meet Meeting' titles.

He again describes his Primal Instinct role to an outside party as contract work rather than employment, and adds the tax classification: 'for the past few months, I've been taking up a 1099, like an independent sales contracting job, and essentially acting as a closer.'
He confirms an active, broad search: 'I am currently applying to multiple jobs, especially, like, just in case' and 'I'm going to apply, or I'm very interested in applying.'

He frames the closer role purely as transferable skill acquisition — 'just learning how to get on the phones, learning how to speak, and like navigate a conversation to the outcome that you want' — with no reference to the product or the clients.

Unlike the Molly Cavanaugh call the previous day, there is no recording disclosure anywhere in this transcript, and the counterparty discusses her employer's internal hiring cadence, headcount, promotion criteria and names two hiring managers.

Corroborates the identity problem in this folder: this speaker graduated college in 2020, is based in Brooklyn and worked at Morgan Stanley and SVB, while the speaker carrying the identical 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' label on every sales call in the same folder is 43 and lives in Krakow, Poland.
